title: Crossing the Rubicon
objective: After this level you can explain why crossing the Rubicon meant civil war.
summary: In 49 BCE Caesar led his army across the Rubicon into Italy: civil war. He beat Pompey at Pharsalus in 48 BCE.

cards.headline: A small river. One step across. No way back.
The boundary
cards.body: The Rubicon was a small river marking the boundary between Caesar’s province and Italy. A general had to leave his army behind before crossing it. In January 49 BCE Caesar crossed with his army anyway. He is said to have declared “alea iacta est”: the die is cast.

cards.headline: Caesar against Pompey
cards.body: The crossing started a civil war. Caesar defeated Pompey at Pharsalus in Greece in 48 BCE. Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered. Today, “crossing the Rubicon” means passing a point of no return.

cards.fact: “Alea iacta est”: the die is cast.
cards.context: Caesar is said to have spoken these words as he crossed the Rubicon in 49 BCE. Once a die is thrown, the throw can’t be taken back.

cards.headline: The Rubicon: crossed
learned: The Rubicon marked the edge of Italy
Caesar crossed with his army in 49 BCE
He beat Pompey at Pharsalus in 48 BCE

questions.prompt: What does “crossing the Rubicon” mean today?

options.label: Winning a battle against the odds
Passing a point of no return

questions.explanation: Caesar’s crossing couldn’t be undone, so the phrase means an irreversible step.

questions.prompt: Why was it illegal for Caesar to cross the Rubicon with his army?

options.label: The river was sacred to Jupiter
Pompey owned the land on the other side
Generals had to leave their armies before entering Italy
Caesar had lost his command in Gaul years before
options.rationale: His army was still with him.

questions.explanation: Bringing an army into Italy was treated as an attack on the state itself.

questions.prompt: From Level 33: which general had already led his army against Rome, in 88 BCE?

options.label: Cincinnatus
options.rationale: He was a model of restraint.

questions.explanation: Sulla’s march on Rome in 88 BCE set the precedent Caesar followed.
